Convert between igraph and graph_data

Source: R/graph-conversion.R
from_igraph.Rd

from_igraph() builds a graph_data() object from an igraph graph. Vertex order is kept, so vertex i becomes node i. Vertex names (or a node_id vertex attribute written by to_igraph()) become node_ids. Numeric vertex attributes named in x_attrs become node feature columns in that order; edge attributes named in edge_attrs become edge feature columns.

Usage

from_igraph(
  ig,
  x_attrs = NULL,
  y_attr = "y",
  edge_attrs = NULL,
  weight_attr = "weight",
  edge_y_attr = "edge_y"
)

to_igraph(g)

Arguments

ig

An igraph object.

x_attrs

Character vector of numeric vertex attributes to use as node features. NULL picks attributes named x_1, x_2, ... if any.

y_attr

Vertex attribute holding node labels (NULL for none). The default uses y when present.

edge_attrs

Edge attributes to use as edge features. NULL picks e_1, e_2, ... if any.

weight_attr

Edge attribute holding weights, used when present.

edge_y_attr

Edge attribute holding edge labels, used when present.

g

A graph_data object.

Value

from_igraph() returns a graph_data object; to_igraph() returns an igraph object.

Details

to_igraph() writes features as attributes x_1, x_2, ... on vertices and e_1, e_2, ... on edges, labels as y and edge_y, weights as weight, and the original identifiers as node_id. With the default arguments, from_igraph() reads these back, so the round trip keeps node order, identifiers, features and their column names, node, edge and graph labels (multi target label matrices as y_1, y_2, ...), weights, types, node and edge masks, graph_attr, metadata and direction. Graph level fields are stored as igraph graph attributes.

For undirected graphs to_igraph() writes each undirected pair once.

Examples

ig <- igraph::make_ring(5)
g <- from_igraph(ig)
g
#> <graph_data> undirected graph: 5 nodes, 10 edges (5 undirected pairs)
ig2 <- to_igraph(g)
igraph::ecount(ig2)
#> [1] 5
